title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Tactile Datasets Boost Dexterous Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
Researchers released several large tactile datasets and fast expert models that dramatically improve real‑world dexterous tasks. Berkeley’s two‑expert architecture couples a high‑level motion planner with a tactile expert four times faster, achieving 65 % success on 12 tasks—about double the best vision‑language baseline. Tsinghua aggregated over 3,000 h of data from 21 sensors into a hardware‑agnostic model, while NeoteAI and USC added visual‑tactile demos and vision‑only pressure inference, raising success rates up to 62.8 %.

### The Caveats
The gains are benchmarked only against a single vision‑language‑action baseline and a generic hardware‑agnostic model, with no comparison to other state‑of‑the‑art tactile methods.

## Rapid In-Hand Pen Writing via Jacobian Estimation

### The Breakthrough
A lightweight CPU‑only controller continuously estimates the combined hand‑object Jacobian online, letting an anthropomorphic hand learn to write with a pen after roughly 18 seconds of initialization. The method requires no analytical model, simulation pre‑training, or demonstrations and attains sub‑millimeter (≤0.6 mm mean) precision on letters and shapes across three different hand platforms.

### The Caveats
The reported accuracy is unconvincing because the work does not compare its Jacobian‑estimation controller to existing RL or imitation‑learning baselines on the same task.

## Contact‑Aware MPC for Aerial Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
The authors fuse nonlinear model predictive control with incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion to control an underactuated quadrotor equipped with a single‑link arm, achieving simultaneous five‑DoF pose and normal‑force tracking on vertical and inclined surfaces without dedicated force sensors, validated on real hardware.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no comparison against existing NMPC or INDI baselines, so robustness and performance gains cannot be verified.

## EVPeriscope: Event‑Camera Quadrotor Localization

### The Breakthrough
An upward‑facing event camera on a ground robot captures the high‑frequency propeller signatures of a nearby quadrotor, enabling 200 Hz closed‑loop relative localization without fiducial markers and remaining robust to motion blur, lighting changes, and foliage in day, night, and wind up to 15 mph.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no quantitative comparison against standard frame‑based or fiducial‑marker methods, leaving reliability claims unsubstantiated.

## Monocular SLAM for Hidden Tomato Detection

### The Breakthrough
By combining GLOMAP’s structure‑from‑motion mapper with a coarse‑to‑fine hierarchical localization strategy, a single inexpensive monocular camera builds a 3D model of greenhouse crops and accurately detects occluded tomatoes, achieving geometric accuracy comparable to manual ground‑truth measurements.

### The Caveats
The paper reports accurate fruit estimates but provides no comparison to existing SLAM or fruit‑detection baselines, so its advantage remains unverified.

## Forester Behavior Trees for Virtual Commissioning

### The Breakthrough
Forester adds a typed language, high‑performance Rust runtime, shared‑state blackboard, and built‑in tracer/simulator, letting engineers script repeatable PLC/robot test scenarios, invariant checks, and fault recovery that run alongside actual PLC logic via HTTP/OPC‑UA.

### The Caveats
The framework is demonstrated only via a descriptive example with no hardware or real‑world testing, so its claimed benefits remain unproven.

## Swarm: Open Arena for AI Drone Navigation

### The Breakthrough
Swarm bundles a unified simulation loop (depth‑camera perception → model → flight commands) running at 50 Hz across 1,100 procedurally generated worlds per epoch, with a token‑based leaderboard and automatic Bittensor rewards for top agents.

### The Caveats
The platform provides no baseline or prior‑art comparisons, so leaderboard scores offer no evidence of improvement over existing drone‑control methods.

## ABot-Recon: Streaming 3‑D Reconstruction

### The Breakthrough
ABot‑Recon reconstructs long video streams into dense 3‑D models using a fixed 12‑frame sliding window, caching KV features and composing adjacent poses to keep compute and memory constant, with pretrained checkpoints and benchmark results included.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no comparison to existing SLAM or reconstruction baselines, so claimed accuracy and throughput gains cannot be judged.

## XPENG Completes Humanoid Robot Production Line

### The Breakthrough
XPENG announced a fully built production line for mass‑producing its humanoid robots, signalling a move from prototype to manufacturing scale.

### The Caveats
The claim rests solely on XPENG’s own announcement with no independent verification, timeline, or technical details.

## RTK Token‑Savings Benchmarks Show Mixed Costs

### The Breakthrough
RTK rewrites shell commands to emit terse summaries, resulting in a 5 % cost reduction for Claude‑based Fable 5.0 but a 5 % increase for DeepSeek V4 Pro across 1,740 attempts, exposing that token‑saving metrics can be misleading for monetary cost.

### The Caveats
Evaluation is limited to Terminal‑Bench 2.1 and two Claude‑based models, leaving performance on newer benchmarks, other LLM families, and real developer workflows untested.

### Priority
The tactile dataset breakthroughs deliver concrete performance gains across multiple labs and directly enable more reliable dexterous manipulation, making them the most actionable start for today’s robotics scan.

### One action
Explore the new tactile datasets and consider integrating Berkeley’s two‑expert architecture into your manipulation pipeline.
